title.narrative: Provision of emergency and sustainable life-saving WASH response packages to drought affected people and or at risk of famine in Burhakaba district

description.narrative: ltpgtFSNAU early warning analysis shows that 3.4 million people experienced acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 or above) in mid-2025, driven by poor rainfall, flooding, and conflict, with the situation projected to worsen to 4.4 million people between October and December 2025 following the failure of the Deyr rains. Bay Region, including Burhakaba District, is among the areas at highest risk, with urban and rural populations expected to deteriorate further as food prices rise and livelihoods weaken.ltbrgtThe drought emergency declared by the Federal Government in November 2025 reflects the severity of the crisis after the fourth consecutive season of below-average rainfall, which has depleted water sources and strained pastoral and agro-pastoral livelihoods. Nationally, 1.85 million children are acutely malnourished, including 421,000 with severe acute malnutrition, placing lives at immediate risk without urgent assistance.ltbrgtIn Burhakaba, food insecurity is closely linked to critical WASH gaps, including non-functional shallow wells, high water prices, limited access to safe water, and reliance on unsafe sources. These gaps have contributed to reported AWD/cholera cases, exacerbating malnutrition and displacement risks. Addressing life-saving WASH needs alongside food and nutrition support is therefore essential to prevent further deterioration and avert excess morbidity and mortality.lt/pgtltpgtIn response to the escalating drought crisis, the proposed project will deliver life-saving WASH assistance to the most drought-affected rural communities in Burhakaba District, improving access to safe water while strengthening hygiene practices and community resilience.ltbrgtThe intervention will include upgrading of 1 strategic borehole, the excavation of three (3) new shallow wells and rehabilitation of seven (7) strategic shallow wells equipped with hand pumps, providing sustainable access to safe water for approximately 5000 direct beneficiaries. To address immediate needs, emergency water trucking will target 12,000 drought-affected people (5,400 women, 3,600 men, 1,800 girls, and 1,200boys) for a period of 60 days, ensuring adequate water for drinking and domestic use.ltbrgtWater quality assurance will be ensured through KRDO’s dedicated water quality team comprising a Water Quality Supervisor and Water Quality Monitors who will conduct routine water quality testing, inspect water trucks, and implement systematic chlorination of water sources. To promote sustainability and community ownership, 1 Water Management Committees (WMCs) will be established and trained on operation and maintenance of rehabilitated water systems.ltbrgtThe project will also support 1,345 vulnerable households through the distribution of hygiene kits, including water storage containers and household water treatment tablets, targeting households receiving emergency water support. This will be complemented by comprehensive hygiene promotion activities, including community and household sessions, campaigns, and targeted trainings to reduce water-borne diseases and improve hygiene behaviors. construction of 76 emergency latrines including 15% disability friendly latrines and purchase and installation of 80 portable solar lampltbrgtThrough these integrated and coordinated interventions, KRDO leveraging its strong operational presence in Burhakaba will address immediate life-saving needs while laying the foundation for medium-term resilience, mitigating public health risks associated with drought and strengthening community capacity for sustainable water management. The population that will be serve by this project are 12,500(5675 women, 3,750 men, 1875 girls and 1250 boys) beneficiaries.ltbrgtlt/pgt
